content:
anya: quick update — ran a short cross-GPU sweep to test a hypothesis: when the kernel selector prefers the paged-flash variant on mixed short->mid seqs we see KV cache eviction spikes and a latency tail. did A100 / H100 / L40S, seq sweep 32 -> 4096, bsz 1 / 4 / 16. posting condensed numbers below.

ci-bot: perf-run queued id=perf-2026-03-17-14:22 pr=4487 (A100,H100,L40S) :rocket:

mike: can you paste the table? tl;dr numbers please — p95 and evict rate

anya: sure — condensed (p95 in ms, throughput tok/s, kv-evict-rate %):
```
GPU    seq  bsz  p95(ms)  throughput tok/s  kv-evict-rate(%)
A100   128   4    18.2      48k               0.9
A100   512  16    32.1      62k               3.4
H100   128   4    17.1      55k               0.7
H100   512  16    74.3      58k               18.9   <-- big tail
L40S    64   1    12.5      30k               1.1
L40S  1024   4   210.8      28k               22.6   <-- kv thrash
```

raj: H100 bsz=16 seq512 74ms is wild — did kernel fallback occur there? looks like memory-related fallback or repeated kvcache evictions. any kernel-selector logs?

lina: also curious if batching heuristics changed the selector (we recently adjusted batch-timeout to 6ms in the canary). could be interplay.

anya: pasted relevant log snippets: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:23:11Z] kernel_selector: choose=paged_flash_v2 reason="latency_budget:low && seq_estimate:mid"
[2026-03-17T14:23:11Z] runtime: launch kernels paged_flash_v2 grid=...
[2026-03-17T14:23:12Z] kv_cache: evict_count+=1245 window_ms=6000
[2026-03-17T14:23:12Z] kernel_runtime: mem_alloc_fallback -> flash_attn (rc=ENOSPC)
[2026-03-17T14:23:13Z] sampler: batch_time=7.2ms cause=wait_full
```

anya: note the sequence: selector picks paged_flash_v2, runtime launches it, eviction ramp then mem_alloc_fallback triggers multiple kernel fallbacks which elongate p95. the eviction window aligns with our new 6ms batch-timeout.

mike: ok — two probable axes: (1) selector aggressiveness for paged_flash on mixed short->mid seqs (2) batching timeout causing larger concurrent KV working set and thrashing.

raj: proposal: run two quick canaries — (A) bump selector seq_floor so fused/flash variant used for seq>=384, (B) reduce batch-timeout to 3ms for this traffic slice and enable kv-prefetch window=256 tokens, observe p95 + eviction. i'll spin them up on H100 + L40S tenant.

lina: add tracer to capture host->device memcpy stalls and kernel queue depth while the run is active. also enable per-request KV hit logging for 1% sample.

ci-bot: perf-run started id=perf-2026-03-17-15:05 canary(A): selector_seq_floor=384, batch_timeout_ms=6000 canary(B): selector_seq_floor=0, batch_timeout_ms=3 kv_prefetch=256

anya: thanks — i'll monitor. if evict_rate drops and p95 compresses we can tune selector heuristic permanently and add metric alarms for kv_eviction_rate > 5%.

mike: good plan. also please capture kernel fallback counts (we want threshold where fallback becomes common).

raj: running now, ETA 20m. will push logs to /tmp/perf-pr-4487 and ping here when done.

anya: noted — tagging @paging-team for visibility :eyes: and will follow up with a short writeup after the canary results.
